cim_eredeti: Pentagon office for AI oversight is understaffed, government watchdog finds
szoveg_eredeti:
Col. Deedrick Reese, deputy commander of the Air Force Sustainment Center, speaks during an artificial intelligence workshop at Tinker Air Force Base, Okla., on July 23, 2026. (Paul Shirk/U.S. Air Force)

The Pentagon office tasked with coordinating the responsible and ethical use of artificial intelligence to better cope with the technology’s swift advances is significantly understaffed, according to a government watchdog.

Staff shortages in the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Office have hindered it from fully implementing the Pentagon’s Responsible AI, the Government Accountability Office said in an Oct. 14 report.

Responsible AI is the Defense Department’s integrated ethical framework for development, deployment and operation of AI capabilities across both combat and non-combat systems.

The office is the lead in matters related to the Defense Department’s adoption and integration of AI, including Responsible AI, the GAO report states.

Staffing shortages, however, have hamstrung the office, with only three of its 10 authorized positions filled as of February, the GAO reported. Defense officials told the GAO that the positions are not likely to be filled.

Rapid AI development has challenged governing bodies around the world as the technology outpaces traditional legislative oversight and human supervision.

Some AI industry leaders have called for slowing the pace of AI advances, warning that loss of control of autonomous AI agents could pose an existential threat to humanity.

“Military decision-making has to be based on human ethics, and just telling a computer to accomplish something may be a very quick way to do it, but it may not be an ethical, moral or legitimate legal methodology to accomplish whatever we’re trying to have happen,” Sean Timmons, an attorney specializing in military law at the law firm Tully Rinckey, said by phone Tuesday.

The military’s use of AI has life-and-death consequences.

Bloomberg reported last month that AI-enabled software used for selecting targets contributed to the U.S. attack on an elementary school with a Tomahawk missile the first day of the Iran War on Feb. 28. More than 100 children were killed.

In February, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and President Donald Trump pressed the AI firm Anthropic to remove safety guardrails in its government-contracted Claude model that prevent it from being used for fully autonomous weapons and mass surveillance.

When Anthropic refused to do so, the administration designated the firm as a national security risk and banned government agencies from using Claude.

The case is being litigated in federal court.

In January, Hegseth issued an AI strategy that “re-emphasized accelerating AI integration and adoption,” according to the GAO report.

“The strategy emphasized a wartime footing, calling for DOD to become an ‘AI first’ warfighting force across all components,” the report states.

The strategy clarified that Responsible AI is to use only models that are free of the type of usage policy constraints posed by Anthropic.

Wyatt Olson is based in the Honolulu bureau, where he has reported on military and security issues in the Indo-Pacific since 2014. He was Stars and Stripes’ roving Pacific reporter from 2011-2013 while based in Tokyo. He was a freelance writer and journalism teacher in China from 2006-2009.

cim: Létszámhiány miatt elakadt az amerikai védelmi tárca AI-etikai ellenőrzése
lead: Az amerikai kormányzati ellenőrző szerv szerint a Pentagon mesterséges intelligenciáért felelős irodája komoly munkaerőhiánnyal küzd.
osszefoglalo:
A [Government Accountability Office](https://www.gao.gov/products/gao-27-107837) jelentése szerint a Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Office nem tudja teljeskörűen megvalósítani a Pentagon felelős AI-keretrendszerét. Az iroda feladata a mesterséges intelligencia etikus és felelős katonai alkalmazásának koordinálása lenne mind a harci, mind a nem harci rendszerekben.

A jelentés rávilágít, hogy a 10 engedélyezett pozícióból mindössze 3 volt betöltve. A védelmi tisztségviselők jelzése szerint a hiányzó álláshelyek betöltése a közeljövőben nem valószínű, ami jelentősen korlátozza az iroda felügyeleti képességeit.

A probléma hátterében az áll, hogy a technológia gyors fejlődése világszerte túlmutat a hagyományos szabályozási és emberi felügyeleti kereteken, miközben a katonai AI-alkalmazások használata kiemelt etikai és biztonsági kockázatokat hordoz.
miert_szamit: A szabályozási és etikai felügyelet hiányosságai **növelik az autonóm AI-rendszerek kockázatait**, ami a vállalati és védelmi fejlesztésekben egyaránt szigorúbb ellenőrzési igényt vetít előre.

prioritas.indok: A Pentagon AI-felügyeleti irodájának létszámhiányáról szóló hivatalos ellenőrzési jelentés.

tenyellenorzes.esemeny: A Government Accountability Office (GAO) jelentése szerint a Pentagon mesterséges intelligenciáért felelős irodájánál (CDAO) tapasztalható létszámhiány akadályozza a felelős és etikus AI-használatot szabályozó keretrendszer megvalósítását.
